name: Break count_rises
expr: (lambda a: isinstance(a, list) and all(type(x) is int for x in a) and sum(1 for i in range(1, len(a) - 1) if a[i] > a[i - 1]) != sum(1 for i in range(1, len(a)) if a[i] > a[i - 1]))(counterexample(1))
show: a = counterexample(1); count_rises(a) must be wrong
why: count_rises stops one pair early: range(1, len(a) - 1) never reaches the last index. It is wrong only when the last value is bigger than the one before it. If your list fails, look at its last two values.

name: Break is_sorted
expr: (lambda a: isinstance(a, list) and len(a) > 0 and all(type(x) is int for x in a) and (a[0] <= a[-1]) != all(a[i] <= a[i + 1] for i in range(len(a) - 1)))(counterexample(2))
show: a = counterexample(2); is_sorted(a) must be wrong
why: This is_sorted compares only the first and last values. Find a list where the ends are in order but a pair in the middle is not, such as a bigger value just before a smaller one.

name: Break first_max_index
expr: (lambda a: isinstance(a, list) and len(a) > 0 and all(type(x) is int for x in a) and max(i for i in range(len(a)) if a[i] == max(a)) != a.index(max(a)))(counterexample(3))
show: a = counterexample(3); first_max_index(a) must be wrong
why: first_max_index moves to every value that is at least as big as the best so far, so on a tie it moves on. It is wrong only when the largest value appears more than once. A list with one largest value cannot break it.

name: Break second_best
expr: (lambda a: isinstance(a, list) and all(type(x) is int for x in a) and len(set(a)) >= 2 and sorted(a)[-2] != sorted(set(a))[-2])(counterexample(4))
show: a = counterexample(4); second_best(a) must be wrong
why: second_best takes the second value from the end of the sorted list. That is wrong when the largest value appears more than once. The list must still have at least two different values.

name: Returns lists of whole numbers
why: Each answer must be a list (not a tuple or a string), so that it meets the input condition of the function it breaks.
